newsitem.title: UK: Jerry Lewis makes London stage debut at 71.
newsitem.headline: Jerry Lewis makes London stage debut at 71.

text.p: Zany comedian Jerry Lewis is making his London stage debut playing the devil in "Damn Yankees" and proving both on and off the stage that he is still young at 71.

"The two worst things that happened to humanity were Hitler and retirement," said the sprightly Hollywood veteran who is taking the musical around the world before ending up on Broadway for a New Year's Eve show on Millenium night.
Lewis, the American star of more than 60 films who is most famed for his double act with Dean Martin, clowned for the cameras on Wednesday and showed there is no age limit on adrenalin.
"If you rest on your laurels as a film man, you atrophy. When you take to the stage, you come alive," he told reporters.

Lewis, who became a great grandfather last year and also has a five-year-old daughter, says of the show that he has played 784 times around the United States: "I wait for 8'clock every night like a kid in a candy store."
After its London run, the musical heads for Paris and Berlin. Then he will be taking it round Canada, Australia and Japan before hitting New York at the turn of the century.
The musical tells the tale of a passionate baseball fan who sells his soul to the devil to become the world's greatest ballplayer.
But, says Lewis, as spry after the show as before: "I would never sell my soul to the devil. I know him too well."
The star whose screen credits include "The Nutty Professor" and "The King of Comedy," said of his nightly performance: "It isn't gruelling at all. Gruelling comes from boredom."

Open heart surgery convinced Lewis that smoking five packets of Gauloise cigarettes a day was not a good idea. He exercises every morning and says: "I will not allow any negativity in my life. That way you stay young and spirited."
